sections.heading: 1. Why We Respire
points: **Respiration** = the process by which **food (glucose) is broken down** in cells to **release energy**.
It takes place in every **living cell** (cellular respiration).
**Breathing** = taking in **oxygen** and giving out **carbon dioxide**; it is part of respiration.

sections.heading: 2. Aerobic and Anaerobic Respiration
points: **Aerobic respiration** — uses **oxygen**; glucose → **carbon dioxide + water + (much) energy**. (Most organisms.)
**Anaerobic respiration** — **without oxygen**; glucose → **alcohol/lactic acid + carbon dioxide + (little) energy**.
**Yeast** respires anaerobically → **alcohol** (used in baking/brewing).
In our **muscles** during heavy exercise, partial anaerobic respiration forms **lactic acid** → causes **cramps**.

sections.heading: 3. Breathing in Humans
points: Air path: **nostrils → nasal cavity → windpipe (trachea) → lungs**.
**Inhalation:** diaphragm moves down, ribs move up/out → chest expands → air in.
**Exhalation:** diaphragm moves up, ribs move down/in → air out.
**Breathing rate** ≈ **15–18 times/minute** at rest (increases with exercise).
In the lungs, **oxygen enters the blood** and **carbon dioxide leaves**.

sections.heading: 4. Respiration in Other Organisms
points: **Fish** breathe through **gills** (extract dissolved oxygen from water).
**Insects (cockroach)** breathe through **spiracles** and a network of air tubes (**tracheae**).
**Earthworms and frogs** can breathe through their **moist skin**.
**Plants** respire through **stomata** (leaves), **lenticels** (stems) and root surfaces — they respire all the time, but photosynthesise only in light.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Respiration = breaking food to release energy (in every cell).
Aerobic (with O₂) → CO₂ + water + more energy; anaerobic (no O₂) → alcohol/lactic acid + less energy.
Yeast → alcohol; muscle cramps → lactic acid build-up.
Human air path: nostrils → trachea → lungs; breathing rate ~15–18/min at rest.
Fish = gills; insects = spiracles/tracheae; earthworm/frog = skin; plants via stomata/lenticels.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Breathing** is only part of **respiration**; respiration (energy release) happens in **cells**.
**Anaerobic** respiration releases **less** energy and makes **alcohol/lactic acid**.
**Muscle cramps** are due to **lactic acid** (anaerobic respiration during heavy exercise).
Insects use **spiracles/tracheae** (not lungs); fish use **gills**.
